reason: Every PROV-JSON fixture under `src/prov/tests/json/` has a file of the same name under `src/prov/tests/provn/provtoolbox-corpus/` or its stem appears in `src/prov/tests/provn/README.md`. The corpus README is the one list of fixtures with no PROV-N counterpart, and the conformance page counts 388 files against it (`docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence).

Reading each file named in `EXCLUDED_PROVTOOLBOX_DOCUMENTS` with the default profile raises `ProvNSyntaxError`, and every key of `IGNORED_EXTENSIONS` and `FAMILY_RECORDS` names a corpus file that is not excluded. The exclusion table of the hand-written documents is the corpus's list of known differences (`docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence), and a stale key in the extension-count tables would hide a renamed or excluded file (#520).

Reading each file named in `EXCLUDED_SPEC_EXAMPLES` with the strict profile raises `ProvNSyntaxError`. The exclusion table of the specification examples is the corpus's list of known grammar differences (`docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence), and an example that starts to parse must leave the table. Some entries record a qualified-name value with an undeclared prefix (#516).

Reading each file named in `KNOWN_DIFFERENCES` gives a document unequal to the PROV-JSON fixture of the same name. The 159 differing files are documented as differences in the generator and not in `prov` (`docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence), so a file that starts to match must leave the table.

Reading each file under `src/prov/tests/provn/provtoolbox-corpus/` outside `KNOWN_DIFFERENCES` with the default profile gives a document equal to the PROV-JSON fixture of the same name. The interoperability claim that PROV-N written by the second implementation reads to the same document as the shared PROV-JSON fixture (`docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence, 229 equal).

Reading each file under `src/prov/tests/provn/provtoolbox/` outside `EXCLUDED_PROVTOOLBOX_DOCUMENTS` with the default profile warns only for its counted dropped extensibility expressions, gives a document with records or bundles, and gives the pinned record count for the two family documents. The second implementation's own hand-written PROV-N documents must parse under the default profile (`docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence), and the Recommendation requires a parser to accept extensibility expressions (#520).

Reading each non-excluded file under `src/prov/tests/provn/spec/prov-n/` and `src/prov/tests/provn/spec/prov-dm/` with the strict profile warns only for its counted dropped extensibility expressions, and re-reading the strict PROV-N written from the result gives an equal document and no warning. The PROV-N and PROV-DM Recommendations' own examples must parse under the strict profile and round-trip (the corpus table on `docs/reference/conformance.md`, Corpus evidence), and the Recommendation requires a parser to accept extensibility expressions (#520).
